images.caption: Figure 1:Server and edge kernel generation follow different optimization regimes.Server methods usually emphasize execution speed within relatively uniform software stacks and generous resource budgets. Edge generation spans fragmented hardware and software ecosystems. It must also balance performance, memory use, and deployment feasibility under tight resource limits.

Figure 2:Overview of EdgeKernelBench.(a)We curate workloads relevant to edge deployment as PyTorch tasks and organize them by compositional complexity and application domain.(b)The LLM uses a layered generation interface to express decisions about graphs, scheduling, and memory. A concrete compiler implementation maps these decisions to execution paths.(c)Each candidate is built, checked against a PyTorch reference program, and timed against a paired baseline.

Figure 3:Overview of LEKA.LEKA organizes layer agents along progressive IR lowering. Their scope narrows from the global program structure to implementation details for a specific target. Compiler conversions preserve prior optimizations while opening search spaces at lower levels. The candidate tree stores IR candidates at different levels and records how they were derived. Hardware feedback guides subsequent search at the relevant level.
